2. Smt. Puja Nishad W/o Shri Subhash Saran Kewat Aged About 33  Years R/o Gali No. 2, Jaidev Bhawan 12, Deepak Nagar Distt. Durg  Civil And Revenue Distt. Durg C.G.
 ---- Respondents For Petitioners : Shri Ajay Mishra, Advocate.

For Respondent No.1/ State : Shri Ajay Kumrani, P.L.
For Respondent No. 2 : Shri Praveen Dhurandhar, Advocate.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey  ORDER 09.11.2023 Heard.

1. The petitioners have challenged the FIR bearing Crime No. 33 of 2021, charge-sheet and order framing charge passed in Criminal Case No. 6199 of 2023 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class Durg (C.G.) for the commission of an offence punishable under Section 498-A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and respondent No.2 would submit that the dispute between the parties has already been settled.

They further submit that the statement of the parties regarding the settlement of the dispute has been recorded before the learned Additional Registrar (Judicial) of this Court on 31.10.2023, where they categorically stated that they have settled the Subhash Saran Kewat vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77153710/
1 dispute and arrived at a settlement without any coercion, greed, or pressure.

sentences.text: 3. From documents, it appears that an FIR was registered against the petitioners for the commission of an offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the IPC.

4. Vide order dated 31.10.2023, petitioners and respondent No. 2 were directed to appear before the Registrar (Judicial)/Additional Registrar (Judicial) of the Registry of this Court on 31.10.2023 i.e.
on the same day for recording their statements.

In pursuance of the above order, petitioner No.1 as well as respondent No.2 appeared before the Additional Registrar (Judicial) on 31.10.2023 and their statements were recorded, where they expressed their desire to enter into compromise without any coercion, greed, or pressure.
5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that the statement of respondent No.2 has already been recorded before the Additional Registrar (Judicial) on 31.10.2023.

He would further submit that as parties have settled their dispute, respondent No.2 does not want to pursue this criminal case any further against all the petitioners and thus, the order for quashment of FIR in Crime No.33 of 2021, charge- sheet and the proceedings of Criminal Case No.6199 of 2023 pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Durg, District Durg (CG) may be passed.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents placed on record.
7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in the matter of 'Ramgopal And Another Vs State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 834' and 'Narinder Singh and Others Vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2014(6) SCC 466', that the matters which can be categorized as personal in nature or in the matter in which the nature of injuries do not exhibit mental depravity or commission of an offence of such a serious nature that quashing of which would override public interest, the Court can quash the FIR in view of the settlement arrived at amongst the parties.

sentences.text: 8. Given the aforementioned facts and circumstances of the case as well as the law rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Ramgopal (supra) and Narinder Singh (supra), and further considering the fact that the petitioners and respondent No.2 have settled their dispute which is evident from the statement recorded on 31.10.2023 before the Additional Registrar (Judicial) of the Registry of this Court, the entire criminal proceedings with respect to FIR dated 14.03.2021 bearing Crime No.33/2021, the charge-sheet and Criminal Case No. 6199 of 2023 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class Durg, District Durg are hereby quashed.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class Durg, District Durg
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove.
